utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom. Could the witness be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blaszczyk. I hope that was the right pronunciation. Please sit down. I would like to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies, and Mr. Thayer has some questions for you, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good morning to you and Judge Nyambe. General Tolimir, Mr. Gajic, good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just wanted to follow-up on a couple of things you said yesterday. I was just going over the transcript last night. At transcript page 1411, line 4, you described the physical collection of these documents, the pick-up of these documents, if you will, from Gornji Milanovac in Serbia. And the transcript, and I'll just quote from the transcript, says: "And it happened, it happened on the night of December 2004," that this commission went to Gornji Milanovac. I just want to ask you, did you mean to say the night of December 2004 or something else?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I meant December 9th, the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, 9 of December.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. When you travelled to Zagreb on 17 December, what was your assignment at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I received task to review -- to make initial assessment of the collection, of the papers. What is in -- whether this is archive of Main Staff or Drina Corps or another unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned yesterday that this process of entering the massive collection by the OTP evidence unit involved assigning ERNs and MIF-ing, I think you said, and then ultimately placing it on the system, to use your term. Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber what you meant when you referred to placing these documents on the system so that everybody could have access to them, as you said before.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that documents after receiving ERN numbers, stamped by ERN numbers, our evidence registration number, were scanned and put in our database. We call it Zyfind. Having these documents in Zyfind, the documents are available for everybody who has, of course, access to the Zyfind, to this database.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does everybody include not just members of the OTP, but members of Defence teams and other authorised folks who represent the accused in these cases?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe if -- yes, if somebody has access or is authorised to have access to this database, yes, has access also to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And have you also heard of the term "EDS"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Evidence Disclosed System, and I believe Defence -- for sure Defence has access to this system.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, is that another form of a database or document retrieval system?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is another form of database.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was the Drina Corps collection ultimately available on this EDS?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back a little bit and ask you some questions about how the collection actually came into being in the first place, not how it arrived at Gornji Milanovac, but how these actual documents were put together to form what we refer to as the Drina Corps collection. Can you share with the Trial Chamber what you've learned through the course of your investigation about how that happened, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, the first information about the collection, how the documents of the Drina Corps were collected, we received from the witness statement, the statement of Nebojsa Vucetic, I think -- Vukovic [sic], sorry, and he told first to the representative of RS in his statement, later on to our investigator, that the collection was -- the papers from Drina Corps units were collected between -- at the end of -- at the beginning of 1996 year until April 1996. Later on, the papers were kept first at Vlasenica command post and in April 1996 were sent to Bijeljina Corps, to the 3rd Corps in Bijeljina, and where the collection was kept there for one year. In May 1997, the collection was again transported from Bijeljina -- from Bijeljina to Sokolac to the premises of the 5th Corps of VRS. And according to this witness, on the order of the Chief of Staff of 5th Corps, at that time Colonel Svetozar Andric, the collection was transported or transferred to Mali Zvornik in Serbia. It was April 1998. According to this witness it was end of April/beginning of May 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just stop you right there if I could, sir. The Trial Chamber's obviously heard references to the Drina Corps and the Drina Corps's subordinate units, the various brigades. You just referred to the 5th Corps. What is the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, after the war the VRS was reorganised and the 5th Corps was created after the war. I believe it was 1997, I think, but I am not sure 100 per cent. But definitely it was after the Dayton Agreement after 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So after the Dayton Agreement at some point, what happened to the Drina Corps itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps was first kept at the command post, as I told, in Vlasenica, then transferred to Bijeljina, and then again transferred, but not to Vlasenica but to the headquarters of the -- to Sokolac. And after -- from Sokolac to Mali Zvornik in Serbia. And in some point, probably about between April 1998 or let's say about spring 1999, the collection was taken somewhere from Mali Zvornik and finally was found again in Gornji Milanovac in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. A couple of things. First is, we need to pause a little bit more, I think, between our question and answer because we're speaking the same language. Second, the question I asked actually was not what happened to the Drina Corps collection, but what happened to the Drina Corps as a military unit after the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Dayton Agreement, Drina Corps was disbanded, and at that place was created 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you told us that in -- sometime in the -- in April of 1998, the decision was taken by General Andric to move the Drina Corps collection from the Republika Srpska across the river to Serbia. Can you share with the Trial Chamber whether you know from your investigation or learned from your investigation why that decision was taken. Did something happen prior to April of 1998 to cause General Andric to make that decision to move these documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1998, in exactly March 1998, the OTP with support of NATO troops in Bosnia, made a search in various locations, in -- it was location in Zvornik Brigade at that time and in Bratunac. And for sure the people who are responsible for archive, they knew that sooner or later we were going to search also in other locations, looking for the documents from this period, from war period, especially we are -- I mean, Srebrenica team was interested at that time about documents from summer 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. What I'd like to do is you've mentioned a couple of locations and just briefly and with Madam Usher's assistance if we can use the ELMO, I want to show you a cut-out from a map. We had thought we could use e-court and one of our map-book maps from e-court, but the resolution simply isn't sufficient. So I've just made a black-and-white photocopy of a portion of P104, and it's from map 1 of P104, the Times Map of the Western Balkans. And I just ask you to -- once we get this up on the ELMO, sir, and I'll give you a green highlighter. If you would, please, just circle Zvornik and you mentioned Mali Zvornik. And if you could just indicate where these locations are and if there's any borders.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should mark it on the screen or --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just on the ELMO version would be better, but that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we can turn that a little bit so we can all read it, please. And can we get a little bit better focus on that. Other way, please. No. Other way, sorry. A little bit more. A little bit more. Zoom out, I think, a little bit -- other way, please. Oh, sorry, yeah, zoom in. If we can get the -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you can just move that map a little bit around so we can see these couple locations on the -- on the screen, that would be helpful. And if you can just start with Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, Mali Zvornik is located across the river, not far from Zvornik, just a few kilometres from Zvornik. I will mark here and encircle this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, if you could just move your microphone a little closer to your face there. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I circled Mali Zvornik and Zvornik area, but as I said, Mali Zvornik is located across the river in the Serbian territory, but Zvornik is still in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record, what river is that that we see separating those two?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could circle Gornji Milanovac, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place is called Gornji Milanovac, is located south of Belgrade about 100, 120, 30 kilometres from Belgrade itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And based on your investigation, the Drina Corps collection, was it recovered actually in the town of Gornji Milanovac or some other location?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was recovered, in fact, in the premises of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro at that time. It was placed -- located very near Gornji Milanovac, in the barracks of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the name of the village was Klaticevo, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll look at some documents and -- but in any event, how close is that village to Gornji Milanovac, for all intents and purposes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say this is one of the suburbs of Milanovac, Gornji Milanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think that we're done with that exhibit, and perhaps we can -- if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would Madam Usher just furnish it to Mr. Gajic and General Tolimir and then hand it up to the Trial Chamber. I think it might have been a little bit difficult to see on the ELMO, and then in the meantime we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We would, upon review by the Defence, tender that cut-out from P104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P00120. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Just a couple more questions and then we'll go through a stack of documents that I have here for you. How many pages approximately is the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps collection consists of about 315.000 pages, plus including -- including, of course, about 360 maps and approximately 3.500 photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, the transcript reflects that you said 315.000 pages, is that the correct number or is it another number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is correct number, because I look at the range of ERN numbers. If we're counting the range, it could be about 315.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during the course of your investigation has the authenticity of this collection been established to you; and if so, how has that been done?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did it through -- mostly through the witnesses. We showed few documents from this collection, some of the documents from this collection, to our witnesses, various witnesses. They recognised the handwritings, the signatures which were put on the papers, particular documents, and also from the statements of the witness -- of the people who testified also in the previous trial. And I can say that this has been established also through our handwriting expert, because few of the documents from this collection were sent to our handwriting expert to make the analysis of that one, to make a report. We got this report, I believe it was 2008, and it was confirmed that the signatures on the documents are authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during the course of your investigation, sir, have you been able to identify other copies of documents which were found in the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we managed to have another copies of some documents from Drina Corps collection. We found these copies also in other collection, like, for example, the VRS Main Staff archive in Banja Luka. I think it was 2008 or 2006. And we got some copies from our witnesses, one of our witness, it was -- yeah, it was the man who was accused by the Tribunal. And we -- as far as I remember, we got also few copies of Drina Corps documents from the Defence of General Krstic during his trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what can you tell the Trial Chamber based, again, on your investigation about how complete the Drina Corps collection is or is not?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am pretty sure we are calling it Drina Corps collection, but I am pretty sure that the collection is not complete because if we look at the sequence order of few documents, the serial number of the particular documents, it's visible that a lot of documents are not in this collection. If we are referring, for example, to security documents and intelligence documents, it's a lot of gaps between the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you find gaps in the series from other organs as well within the Drina Corps and other units?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's not only in regards to the security and intelligence documents, but also to operational documents, to logistic documents, and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you able to determine whether any particular date ranges, for example, were missing from the collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that the most significant period where -- I was interested, of course, in Srebrenica events, the most significant period where the documents are missing, where we cannot find anything about particular events and we see the gaps between the documents, it was July 1995 and later July, August, and September till October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, before this Drina Corps collection was removed from Gornji Milanovac in 2004, who had access to the Drina Corps collection while, for example, it was in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that the Defence of -- probably Defence of General Krstic had access to this collection when it was probably collect -- placed in Mali Zvornik -- sorry, in Mali Zvornik. And also from one of the witnesses who testified in this Tribunal, we know that General Miletic had also access to this collection. And this witness who testified in the previous trial, but I think he was protected witness, he testified that he got access to the collection as well. According to this witness, General Miletic was in Mali Zvornik in the spring 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And just so there's no mystery about it, if we may go into private session, Mr. President, for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, for the remainder of the examination, let's go through some documents. The first one I'd like to show you is 65 ter 2034, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but I have no broadcast of --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's -- there it is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. What we have here is a document dated the 8th of December, 2004, from the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence, a decision, and it refers to a commission being appointed. What is this commission, sir, that's referred to here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is commission appointed for taking over and handing over the archive material the Army of Republika Srpska located in Serbia, in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And these gentlemen by the surnames of Matic, Radisic, and Sisic, who are they members of?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of this commission appointed by the Minister of Defence, Milovan Stankovic. They were appointed as the members of the commission, but Colonel Mirko Matic became the president of this commission. And they were responsible for taking over and handing over the archive material.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Are they army or are they MUP?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, the court reporter asked us this morning before we started if you could -- if there could be more of a pause between our question and answer.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thanks. And I'll do my best, too. And we're done with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could take a look at 65 ter 2036, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we have here a decision dated the 8th of December, 2004, again from the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence. Can you just tell us what this decision concerns.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is decision of approval of the official trip for the president of the commission, Mirko Matic, lieutenant-colonel. Approval for the trip to abroad, you know, to just collect this documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does it say about when this trip is supposed to happen?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decision was issued on the 8th of December, 2004, but the official trip should take place on the 9th -- 9 of December, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 2035, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we have here a document headed "General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska," dated 8 December 2004. First I just have a question for you, if you know. The Trial Chamber has certainly heard many references to the Main Staff of the VRS. And here, in 2004, we see a reference to the General Staff. Can you just explain the difference, if you know.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, this is difference between the name, but I think that general -- the Main Staff of VRS, the name has been changed --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- sometime after -- I don't know, it was after the Dayton Agreement or after August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you just tell the Trial Chamber what this document is about, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is more or less the same contents of the previous -- as the previous document. This is order for official trip for the -- issued for the members of the commissions -- for the three members of the commission. And it's saying here that the commission, the people listed in this order, should travel to Belgrade on 9 December 2004 to execute the task. And this order is signed by the Chief of General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And I would just note, sir, that you said it was signed by the Chief of the General Staff. If we're looking at the original version in Cyrillic --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am looking at the original version.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Because we have a translation here that says "head of the Main Staff," but that Cyrillic word is the word for "chief"; is that correct? That's the correct term, not "head"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would translate it as a chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, may we have 2037, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Here we have a -- what's headed as a record, and on the top half it's dated the 8th of December, 2004, and it's generated by the General Staff of the VRS. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is about, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is kind of the receipt prepared by General Staff by -- of the Army of Republika Srpska. And this receipt, in fact, was prepared on the 8th of December, 2004, but if we look at the original, we see that it has been signed on the 9th of December, 2004. This is a receipt of the receiving of the archive material, which was located in the village of Klaticevo, it is a village located very near to Gornji Milanovac. And we see in the bottom of this original document the signature of Dragan Brcan, who was a member of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro who handed over the archive material to the commission. And we have the names and signatures of the members of the commission, Mirko Matic, Dragan Radisic, and Miljan Sisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And there's a reference to 16 crates; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a reference to the 16 cases of the archive materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- ask a question. I didn't understand your comment about the date, that in the original there's some reference to the 9th of December, 2004. I don't see that. Could you explain that a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is -- as I said, this document was prepared the day before, on the 8th of December, 2004, but I believe next, just above the signature of Dragan Brcan, is the date, 9 of December, 2004. It means that the archive was collected on the 9th of December, 2004. In fact, this document, without signature, of course, has been prepared the day before the material was collected or handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And below the headline I see the date of 8th December 2004. Thank you very much. Please carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May we have 65 ter 2031, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before this will be removed, Mr. Tolimir wants to raise something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace to this house and to everybody following this trial; may God help you all. I wanted to say something about the record. If you look at the heading of the document, in the Serbian version we can see the year 2000, and in the record it says 2004. Could that mistake or that error be removed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think the document speaks for itself, and I think we should just leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think this is just an omission to put a number 4 to it. It's not 2000 but 200 and then there is a gap, if you look at that. But you may deal with this during cross-examination. Please carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May we have 65 ter 2031 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we -- we're looking at a document and it appears, unfortunately, we don't have a translation of this document. Let me just double-check. I'll just take you through some of the pages and keep the information pretty simple, so I think that will help matters a little bit. If we look at this first page here, there's a name in -- well, first of all, please tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is declaration of receipt of the materials. This declaration was prepared by our investigator on the -- from the Sarajevo field office, in fact, from the Banja Luka field office. His name is Finn Tollefsen. He's saying that he received 16 sealed and padlocked boxes from Mr. Dragi Milosevic, who was at that time the head of police administration, I believe, criminal police administration of Republika Srpska. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And -- sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the material, the 16 sealed and padlocked boxes were received by Finn Tollefsen on the 13th December 2004. And we have signature of Dragi Milosevic and I believe this is handwriting of Finn Tollefsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say we have the signature of Dragi Milosevic, can you tell the Trial Chamber who that person is, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told, he was the head of police -- criminal administration of the police of Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "police," is it fair to say we can also refer to him as MUP?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can refer to him as member of the Ministry of Interior defence, a MUP member.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this, basically, two-day operation by the RS authorities to recover these documents from Serbia, can that be described as a co-operative operation between the RS MUP and the RS army; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is fair to say according to our information and the information that we received from Ministry of Defence of -- and Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska. It was joint operation. In fact, the members of Ministry of Defence, they received information where their archive is stored, when they're supposed to take this archive, but members of the Ministry of Interior, they facilitated the travel of this documentation or transport of this documentation to Bosnia from Gornji Milanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, I'll try to keep the questions a little simpler, bearing in mind we only have the English version here. If we look at the very bottom of the document, in the handwritten portion, we see the initials "EOD" --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- after the reference to the 16 boxes. What's "EOD," sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Finn refers here to Explosive Ordnance Devices team. It was not NATO team or EUFOR team at that time who checked all the boxes for the possible explosives placed in these boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then we see a reference to the boxes being repacked into 24 other boxes. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what that's about, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Finn Tollefsen mentioned here that the contents of 16 boxes were repacked into 24 cardboard boxes, but I would say that this is not fully correct because in the meantime, on the 14th of December, 2004, Finn received also from Dragi Milosevic, from the members of MUP of Republika Srpska, another box containing the audio-tapes and videotapes seized by the Republika Srpska MUP in other operation. But this -- the contents of these boxes, audio-tapes and videotapes, has nothing to do with this Drina Corps collection. But also I see Finn here also repacked this box to -- we can count, together with the 16 boxes with Drina Corps collection, into 24 cardboard boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to the next page, if we could, of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could -- is it perhaps possible for a better understanding for the accused that the handwriting -- handwritten part at the bottom of this page could be read out in English so that we have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you would comply with His Honour's request, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 16 boxes were EOD'd on the 15th/16th December 2004 and thereafter re-packed into 24 cardboard boxes." "Banja Luka 16 December 2006," the name of Finn Tollefsen, investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you sure that this is 2006?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, no, this is -- in fact, this is 16 December 2000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 200, in fact. This is not clear here. This is copy of the document, I think it could be the copy or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think in the second line at the beginning, we have a reference to 2004.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we may just turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, sir, and to pick up on His Honour's direction, if you would just read what this is and perhaps just that first line there into the record and just tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is statement of enclosure, and it's written here: "I, hereby, certify that I received one sealed diplomatic bags/container from ICTY Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And -- sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And is receiving pouch officer Thomas E. Osorio is head of UN ICTY Liaison Office in Zagreb, Croatia, his signature and date, 17 December 2004, 1630 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we look down on the second lower half of the document, there's some remarks and it indicates that on 17 December 2004, the Zagreb Liaison Office received 24 cardboard boxes and that they were then inspected and repacked into 57 boxes. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what that's all about.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when the boxes arrived to the Zagreb field office on the 17th December 2004, I was present at Zagreb field office at that time. I already arrived to the Zagreb, and we decided to repack these boxes into 27 -- into smaller boxes, in fact, because the boxes used to transport for the documents were too heavy and were parting apart -- just was falling apart. And during these two days, 17, 18, and I believe it was 19, we -- I checked personally the contents, roughly, the contents of the documents of the boxes, and we repacked these 24 cardboard boxes which arrived from the ICTY field office in Banja Luka, including the box containing the tapes and audiotapes from other operation. And we repacked the contents of these 24 cardboard boxes to another boxes, 27 boxes, which includes two boxes containing the tapes and audiotapes seized by Republika Srpska MUP in other operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Again, sir, just so the record is clear, you said they were repacked into 27 boxes. Is that the correct number or is it a different number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is 27 -- 57, sorry, I meant 57 boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we may just turn the page quickly and we'll be done with this document shortly. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, please, and we won't need to dwell too long on it.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is kind of table we prepared during the repacking the contents of the -- during the repacking the boxes which arrived from Banja Luka field office into new 20 -- 57 boxes -- 55 boxes, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what I just wanted to ask you about. We have at the top here, you see a reference to 23 big cardboard boxes and you just talked about 24 boxes. Can you account for the difference, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I'm referring here to the boxes containing the documents from the Drina Corps collection. I didn't count the box of audiotapes and videotapes seized by Republika Srpska MUP in different -- totally different operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we just turn the page one more, please. We see the number 55 in the middle of the page. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is referred to the boxes, "55 kutije." I think, B/C/S this is "box" or "case."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may have the next page, please. And you know what, we can just skip this particular page and if we could have the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What is this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a packing list. In this packing list we have -- we have description what was in transport which was provided from the Zagreb field office to The Hague. And here we have description of "evidence documents from Banja Luka" and "evidence tapes from Banja Luka." And we see here that it was 55, number 55, which means 55 boxes, and number 56/57 means boxes containing evidence tapes from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 2033, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have a photograph here. What is it, sir, and who took it, if you know.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was taken by my colleague from the field office from Banja Luka, by Finn Tollefsen, in describe -- depicting here one of the boxes seized or received in Gornji Milanovac. And the documents which probably were in this box, this crate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you there while this photograph was taken, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This photograph was taken in Banja -- in our Banja Luka field office, but I was not present. But later on we received the CD containing about 30 photographs from Finn Tollefsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may have 65 ter 2032, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, same three questions: What is it and who took it and were you there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is one of the photos taken by Finn Tollefsen in Banja Luka field office, and we see here one of the boxes used for transporting of the documents. And -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And were you there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take a look at some of the documents which were generated by the Republika Srpska and by the Serbian government in 2004 and 2005 in connection with this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may start with 2029, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What we have here is a Republika Srpska MUP document dated 20 December 2004. And it's directed to the ICTY OTP office in Banja Luka, the subject being the VRS Main Staff archives. And again, first of all there's a reference here to the Main Staff archives. Did your investigation disclose whether this collection was a Main Staff archive or some other archive?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the contents of the documents seized at that time and after analysis of these documents, we see that this is not Main Staff collection, this is Drina Corps collection and documents regarding the units subordinated to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just focusing on the first paragraph of this document, there's a reference here, and I quote: "... the Republika Srpska minister of interior, through his previous official contacts with the SMN Ministry of Defence and the head of the General Staff of SMN army, initiated and intensified delivery of mentioned archives ..." And it refers up above to the VRS Main Staff and Drina Corps archives. First of all, what's "SMN" stand for, those three initials?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means Serbia and Montenegro army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And there's a reference here, as I just quoted, to "previous official contacts." What did your investigation disclose or learn about these previous official contacts?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know from the -- from a few documents we received later on from RS that the Ministry of Interior, delegation of the Ministry of Interior had a few meetings in Serbia. I think it was October 2004. And during the meetings one of the subject of the, let's say, talks with authorities of Serbia, it was the archive who possibly can be located on the territory of Serbia at that time. The meeting took place, I think, in Belgrade, and it was meeting between representative -- between Ministry of Interior, members of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska and Ministry of Defence of Serbia and I think between also the people from the Main Staff of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro at that time. And during this meeting in October 2004 has been decided that if there is any archive exists on the territory of Serbia, it should be returned to Bosnia, to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we just flip to, for example, page 3 of the English, and that's also page 3 of the original Cyrillic, we see a lot of black, redaction. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what that's about, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we redacted this part of these documents because this part had nothing -- is not related to the archive but is related to another operation conducted by MUP and I believe by -- yes, mostly by MUP and, as far as I remember, also by SFOR troops in co-operation with MUP in relation to another operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly requested to slow down and pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'll try to slow down and pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may have 65 ter 2030, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We have another MUP document, this one dated 10 January 2005, this time from the crime -- translated here as crime police administration. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what this document generally speaking is, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document described the way how -- how Republika Srpska authorities located and transported and received the Drina -- the archive -- the war-time archive and transported this archive to Banja Luka. They referring to the archive handed over to them on the 9th of -- on the 9 of December, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, and in general, does this cover the same information as the document we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this cover the same information we looked before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's just flip to the last page, page 4 of the English, please, and that is page 3 of the Cyrillic version.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the larger paragraph in the middle of this page there's a reference to "... MUP members received this information from representatives of the Ministry of Defence through their negotiation and collaboration channels, the said representatives had made it possible for the archives to be loaded and driven out of the barracks." What does this reference to "negotiation and collaboration channels" and "information" refer to, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information refers to the information I already -- to information -- or to the events I already talk a few minutes before, about the meeting which took place in October 2005 -- 2004, sorry, in Belgrade. The meeting which took place -- the people who were at the meeting were the members of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska, Ministry of Defence of Serbia and Montenegro, and members of the Army of the Main Staff of the Army of Montenegro -- Serbia and Montenegro. And during this meeting there was discussion about the archive, but more detailed information was received by the members of Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska from the Ministry of Defence and Army of Serbia. The information whereabouts of the archive and they received the information when and where exactly these archives should be collected by the commission appointed by the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And is it -- is it fair to say then that there had been information received prior to this meeting in October of 2004 through these channels? Is that how it works, sir, and that information was then brought up at this meeting? Or was the information disclosed for the first time in the meeting, if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 5427, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have here, sir, a document dated 7 of March, 2005, and it's headed at the top "The Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency, office number 2 for co-operation with the ICTY in The Hague." And it's -- this cover letter is signed by Trivun Jovicic. Who was he, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the ICTY liaison officer. He works for, of course, for the Government of Republika Srpska, and he's liaison officer with ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this is enclosing a letter - and we'll just turn the page, please, to the next page - and this is dated -- a letter dated 3 March 2005. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is response for our RFA. We asked authorities of Republika Srpska some information regarding the collection itself, it means how, when, and who participated in the movement of this collection first from Bosnia to Mali Zvornik, then to Gornji Milanovac, and also who collected -- who participated -- I believe, who participated of -- how the collection was returned to Bosnia again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, and you referred to an RFA. What is an RFA?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Request For Assistance. Any time if you would like to get any information from any of the governments or some institutions, we are preparing the request for the assistance. And in this request we are asking them to undertake the certain action or asking them for certain information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on this document we have a reference to another case, the Prosecutor versus Slobodan Milosevic. And what's that about, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see from the initials that this RFA had been prepared by one of my colleagues who worked at that time for Milosevic case, and in fact, this collection -- the documents from this collection were used not only by Srebrenica teams but also by other teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to page 3 of the English, please, and that will be pages -- the bottom of page 2 of the B/C/S and then continue on into page 3 - I'm sorry - of the Cyrillic. We see in this response -- I'll just wait until we get page 2 of the Cyrillic up. And at the bottom of -- yeah, the bottom of that page, going up to page 3 of the Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have references here to information and findings by the RS Ministry of Defence and the references to the archives being transported in the spring of 1998. And we see here a reference to the transport and hand-over of the archived material, again this is referring to the spring of 1998, was done by Sergeant Nebojsa Vukicevic. Who was that person, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person was the member of the Army of Republika Srpska. He was responsible for the archive. He is the person -- I referred to this person some time ago when I talked about the information we received regarding the whereabouts of this archive between 1996 and 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we see further down that there's a reference to Lieutenant-Colonel Dragan Obrenovic. And what does he have to do with this operation, according to the information that you received?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to information I received, and there were two sources, in fact, they were information from Dragan [sic] Vukicevic and another information from the protected witness which was -- which name was mentioned in private session, that the archive, the first half spring 1998, was transported to Zvornik and to Mali Zvornik -- and then to Mali Zvornik and was located in the facilities of Army of Serbia and Montenegro. And he says that was led -- in this document it says that the transportation was led personally by the commander of the 503rd Motorised Brigade, Colonel Dragan Obrenovic. But we know from the protected witness that Dragan Obrenovic, in fact, facilitated the transport of this archive, in fact, the passage of this archive through the border. Because, as we know, Mali Zvornik is located in Serbia, across the river, Drina river, from Zvornik. He facilitated the passage of this archive, the bus, the truck who arrived with the archive, together with -- escorted by Sergeant Nebojsa Vukicevic and -- yes, and he helped them to pass the border and to facilitate them to locate this archive in Mali Zvornik. And from my -- our investigation we know that Nebojsa Vukicevic was assisted also by Dragan Savic. He was assistant commander for the security of the 503rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, we've -- you've just mentioned the 503rd Motorised Brigade. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what relationship, if any, there is between the Zvornik Brigade and the 503rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that, I would like to take you back to page 28 of the transcript, line 15. You mentioned the name Dragan Vukicevic. Are you sure that you combined the first and the second name correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, of course, I meant Nebojsa Vukicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, may I have a transcript on my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It disappeared from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That it's clarified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you recall the question of Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure. What is the relationship, if any, between the Zvornik Brigade and the 503rd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After reconstructing the Army of Republika Srpska, the Zvornik Brigade was disbanded and in this place was created 503rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when approximately would this have happened?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it happened after the Dayton Agreement, in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may turn the page in English to page 4, and I think we can stay on page 3 of -- or, yeah, page 3 of the Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We see the top three paragraphs here and they refer to a meeting on 15 October 2004, to a meeting in Belgrade. And what is this about, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about the meeting I referred before when -- meeting between Ministry of Interior delegation of Republika Srpska, regarding the meetings with representative of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro and representative of the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Serbia. In this meeting, as we see here in this document, was discussed also the issue about archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're done with that document. May we see 65 ter 6220, please. And if we could go to page 2 of the English. We can stay where we are on the Cyrillic, but if we could just go to page 2 so we can see where the -- what the source of this document is in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's not the same page in Cyrillic and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. President. If we could have the second page of the Cyrillic, please, and that will have -- that will bear the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This -- can you just tell the Trial Chamber, please, what this document is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also response for our RFA, but we directed this RFA to the Government of Serbia and Montenegro, with the same question regarding the Drina Corps archive, how, when, who participated in the movement of this archive from Bosnia to Serbia and Montenegro, what was the reason, these type of the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in general, how did this response correspond or not with the response that the OTP received from the authorities in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information -- yeah, this is -- if we look at information we receive of -- from Republika Srpska, it more or less the same information, that the archive was transferred from Bosnia and Herzegovina to Mali Zvornik in April 1998. And in fact, according to this information we received from authorities of Serbia and Montenegro, it was done without knowledge of the supervising officers of these particular units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "units," you mean units of Republika Srpska or units of Serbia and Montenegro, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean units of Serbia and Montenegro army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just one last question on this document. If we look at the very top of the English, there's a reference again to a meeting on 15 October 2004. Is that the same meeting that's -- that you've been talking about and that we've seen - and I'll try to slow down, sorry - and that we've seen in some of the other documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same meeting I referred before and also the same meeting which was described in the document received from Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you referred in your earlier testimony to a statement being provided by this individual by the name of Nebojsa Vukicevic. Again, to whom did he give his statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- Nebojsa Vukicevic, he gave a statement to the commission created by the army -- by authorities of Republika Srpska, Bosnia-Herzegovina, but also one of our investigators met Nebojsa Vukicevic in some stage. During this meeting he had confirmed his statement given to the authorities of Republika Srpska regarding the archive, movement of the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may have 65 ter 2158, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is statement of Nebojsa Vukicevic I referred before -- to which I referred before. It was given to the authorities -- to the commission of Republika Srpska. And also in this statement he describing the movement of Drina Corps archive between the period of 1996 up to 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may go to page 2 of the English, please, and page 2 of the Cyrillic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There's a reference here to General Krstic on April 7th of -- well, General Krstic ordering the removal of certain documents which was carried out on the 7th of April, 1996. What do you know about this, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- I -- sorry. I know, according to this statement we received this information also through -- from Nebojsa Vukicevic, that General Krstic took out few documents from the collection, from Drina Corps collection. It was documents of the Krivaja 95 and document with the code-names Spreca 95. This is operation regarding Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I think you referred earlier in your testimony to members of the Krstic Defence team having access to the archives, if my memory serves. You referred at some point to that. Is that what this is referring to or is that a different occasion when people had access to the archives?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir's microphone be turned off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please switch off your microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. This reference here to documents being removed upon General Krstic's order in April of 1996, is that the same occasion that you referred to earlier, I believe, with respect to members of General Krstic's Defence team having access to the Drina Corps or is it different?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to different documents. I saw different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at one more document before the break, please, 65 ter 2170.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we only have an English version of this document, unfortunately, but I'll just ask you a general question about it. What is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is receipt of the material we received from the Defence of General Radislav Krstic. The receipt was issued on the 19th February 2000, and in this receipt we have listed documents which -- in fact, copy of the documents which we received -- I mean, OTP received from the Defence of General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when we come back from the break, I'll ask you some follow-up questions about that document, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, you have shown us a series of documents. I just would like to know if you are tendering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I thought I'd save that until the end of the exercise and then just race through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. We must have our first break now. We adjourn and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know if we still have 2170 up on the screen. If not, can we have 2170, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Before the break, sir, you told us that this is a receipt for documents that were given to the OTP by the Krstic Defence team. What I want to do is show you copies of some of the documents, just three actually, that are listed on this receipt. And the first one I want to show you is the document at number 4, and I'll just read it into the record. It says that it's a Main Staff VRS, order number 03/4-1670 from 17 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what I'd like to do and ask the assistance of the court staff in this is show two B/C/S originals side by side in e-court. We don't need the English translations because I won't be going into the substance of the documents. I merely want to be able to show the witness different copies of the same document which we have in e-court. So if we could have 65 ter 778 and 65 ter 2173 side by side in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We see here we have two documents bearing the report number or strictly confidential number, as it's translated, 03/4-1670, that's the report number that we just saw on the receipt. Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, without going into what the substance of these documents are, just can you tell them about what the source of either of these documents is.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contents of these documents -- in fact, this is one original and another copy of the original of this document. But looking at the ERN number of the documents on my screen, on the right side, starting with 0425, I see this is document from the Drina Corps collection, the document on the right side from my screen. And I believe this is the original. And that one on the left side, it should be copy of the document from the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how can you tell by looking at the ERN that this is a document from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know, I am aware, about the range of Drina Corps collection. The range started from our number, Evidence Registration Number, from 0425, 00, onwards. We should keep in mind that there were about 315.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And you just told us that you believe that the Drina Corps document on the right is the original and that the one on the left which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we can just scroll down a little bit on the one on the left, please, I think there should be an ERN at the top. I'm sorry, scroll the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The one on the left bearing ERN 00917857, what was the source of this document, sir, this copy of the original?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seen description of this document on the previous evidence document under the point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe this is document -- the copy of the document we received from Krstic Defence. But here regarding the document from Drina Corps collection, of course, I am -- right now I am guessing that this is original document but I am pretty sure. But I think it is quite easy to check it, just getting this document out from evidence vault.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "original document," what do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean document prepared by the men or people who just issued this document or just prepared this document, and it was done on the time when document was prepared was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So by what you just said, does the Drina Corps collection then also include some copies of documents as well as originals of documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this collection there are so many pages that it's possible that there were copies also.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "copies," are you referring to photocopies or different versions of the same document that were received by other units who were receiving or who had -- who had been the recipients of -- let me just stop and start over again. When you say "copies," sir, do you mean photocopies or multiple copies of the same document which were distributed to numerous recipients, or both, or something else? If you could explain, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean both version. It could be that photocopies but also the multiple copies of the same documents which was sent or resent to various units of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we may see some examples of that shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at and do the same side-by-side comparison, please, with 65 ter numbers 2172 and 2171, please. Okay. Thank you for blowing that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have here two documents which bear the strictly confidential number 04/156-9. Can you tell us anything about the source of these two documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we see on the screen, the document on the right side with ERN number stamp on this document 04367235, this is the range of the Drina Corps collection. And this is -- I believe this is original document. And the document on the left side of the screen, this is copy of the same document we have on the right side. I saw previously the ERN number. I believe this is also document -- I mean, the copy of that document we received from Krstic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just for the record, the document on the left bears ERN 00917861.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's do the same exercise with just one more set of documents. If we may have 65 ter 2174 and 1982 side by side, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have here two documents which bear the strictly confidential numbers of 03/156-11. What can you tell us about the sources of these documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, but right now the document on the left side of my screen with ERN number 04312743, this is Drina Corps collection document, and I believe this is original. And on the right side this is the copy of the document from Drina Corps collection, the same document but the copy, having ERN 00917878 or 9, I don't see clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we just go to page 2 of 65 ter 1982, we'll see what the ERN is there. And we see that page 2 bears the ERN of 00917879. And again, sir, just to move things along, this version, was this one of the documents that was provided to the OTP by the Krstic Defence?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I believe this is document -- the copy of the document provided to OTP by Krstic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We're done talking about the documents that appeared on that receipt from the Krstic Defence. Let's look at some other examples of some other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 2023 on the screen, please, and 4047B, side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We have two documents, both bearing the strictly confidential number 04-520-54/95. And we can see that both documents have the first four numbers 0425 as part of their ERN. What can you tell us about these documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell that both documents are coming from the same collection, from Drina Corps collection, looking at the ERN numbers of these documents. And I can say that the document from the left side, at least that one, was in the possession of Rogatica Brigade because on the top right corner of this document I see the signature of Ziza. Ziza, this is communication officer from Rogatica Brigade. We interview him and he recognised his handwriting of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that may -- well, I believe that that is written in Cyrillic, so if you could just identify where on the document that is. Is it right underneath the number, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's just underneath the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what's the number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Cyrillic. 1726.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look at the document on the right, 65 ter 4047B, is there a stamp on the lower right-hand corner and what does that stamp signify, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the command of 5th Mixed Artillery "Puk," I think. In B/C/S, of course. This is information that this document was received on the 15th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that would be received by that unit that you just referred to; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at two more documents with the same strictly confidential number, the same, those are 65 ter 4047C and 65 ter 125, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, we see a stamp on the document on the right, and it's at the bottom left-hand corner of 65 ter 125. Can you tell us about that stamp, please. Can you read it or do you need it blown up?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would it be possible, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could blow up, there's a stamp at the far left corner. Perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. This is a stamp of the command of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, saying us that this document had been received by the Zvornik Brigade on the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's just take a look at the typesetting on these two documents. It appears, for example, on the document on the left, 4047C, we have almost everything in capitals, and then on the right we have almost everything in small-case letters. Can you just explain and account for why the same document has different -- different lettering or casing or appearance even though it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's visible that this document was sent to various units, including the command of the Zvornik Brigade, and probably Zvornik Brigade they had different type of machine that they received this document. It was typed in this way. But on the left side we see -- I don't know which unit received this document, but also type -- yeah, this is visible that they were different type of teleprinter or other machine used to receive these dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Are you -- for the witness. My question is for the witness. Are these two documents one a copy of the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, that this is multiple copy. It's not exactly copy, but this is document sent from Main Staff -- or sent from the 1st Podrinje Brigade to various units. The first was Zvornik Brigade, another one was -- I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or -- may I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it's possible that this document, because I don't see the stamp at the bottom of this document, was typed in the Zvornik -- or in the Podrinje Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then resent to the various units of the Drina Corps units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And let me just follow-up on Judge Nyambe's question if I could and we will have other more technical witnesses who will be able to explain this whole process.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But, sir, just basically, can you explain how documents are transmitted from one unit, say a subordinate unit, out to the -- I'm sorry, a superior unit out to the subordinate units and how that would explain different copies of the same documents having a slightly different appearance even though it's the same document. If you can just explain, based on your knowledge, how that works and why we see the same document looking a little different when it's received by other units.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Transferring documents to the various units, it could be done in various ways, in fact. It could be done through the telephone, through the secure line, and this is why -- for example, the documents is dictated on the phone to the operator in other unit who's supposed to receive this document, and operator is typing out the contents of the document. The recipient also can receive document on the teleprinter, which is used by this particular unit. It's more or less the same. And this is why we have various type of letters in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So if a communications officer in the Zvornik Brigade is receiving the same document that somebody in the Vlasenica Brigade might be receiving, they'll look different because their respective machines that are typing these things out for them as they're coming in might just have different type-face settings or something like that. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, how were these -- well, let me just ask it this way. Were there, to your knowledge, means or mechanisms by which these communications were encoded or encrypted? And I don't want to get into an in-depth analysis because we'll have other people, but just can you tell the Trial Chamber whether that was done; and if you know, just basically how that was done.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some messages can be encrypted, of course, but if -- in this way that another unit should have the device, with encrypted device, in fact, who could decrypt the receiving document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, in July, for example, of 1995, did various VRS units also have just basic fax capability as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have the basic fax capability as well and they have also communication line, I mean telephone line. They may use these communication telephone lines. It could be civilian lines or it could be military lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move through some other examples, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 182 and 4046B, Bravo, side by side, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We have two documents, each bearing the strictly confidential number 04-520-53/95. What can you tell us about these two documents, sir, and their sources?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two documents are coming from the same collection, from Drina Corps collection, looking at their ERN numbers. And also I notice on the document on the left side with ERN number 04258575, the initials of Ziza, the communication officer from Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, just to move things along, that's underneath the number 1726; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the number now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We need to scroll down a little bit on the other -- on the document on the left, please. On the document on the left we need to just scroll down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, this is under the number 1726.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to direct your attention to the lower right-hand corners of each of these documents, and just generally, what do you see there? What does that in your experience -- what do those markings represent?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On both. We see -- we see handwriting and numbers on the lower right-hand corners of both documents, and what are those?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwritings we see on the -- this document on the right side with ERN number 04258627, we see that this document was received by particular unit on the 14 July 1995. I think at 2035 hours and the number of the document. And signature of the person who received this document. On the left corner in the bottom, we have initials of the man who prepared, who typed out, this document I believe, it's D.ZZ. I think it could be initials of this communication officer from the Rogatica Brigade, Desimir Zizovic. They called him Ziza.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we see 65 ter number 180 side by side with 65 ter 4043B, please. And we have two documents bearing strictly confidential number 04-520-52.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the sources of these two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we can scroll down just a little bit on the one on the right, please, so we can catch the ERN at the top. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. I see from ERN number that this is -- that these two documents are coming from different sources. The first one, that one on the left side with ERN number 04258572, comes from Drina Corps collection.
