The one on the right on my screen with ERN 05296337, I think that this document comes from Banja Luka VRS archive collection. And also looking at the first document with the initials of Ziza and on the top right corner of this document and initials on the bottom on the left D.ZZ., I believe this document was prepared by Desimir Zizovic from Rogatica Brigade and was sent from Rogatica Brigade to various units of Drina Corps. And looking at the document on the right side of my screen with ERN number 05296337, I don't see clearly the stamp here, but if I --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we can scroll up just a little. I don't know if there's any more information on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see clearly which unit received this document, but it's visible that it was received from the 14th July, approximately about 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 2025 and 4048B side by side. I think everybody will be happy to know we're coming towards the end of this particular exercise. Just a couple more examples. Okay. We have two documents bearing strictly confidential numbers 04-520-55/95.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about these two documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two documents were sent -- I mean that they are coming from the same collection, from Drina Corps collection. And I see the document from the left side -- I would say that it would be document prepared by teleprinter operator in Rogatica Brigade and sent from Rogatica Brigade to other units of Drina Corps -- I mean, it was directed to the sector for intelligence and security, Main Staff, and Drina Corps, and IKM of Drina Corps. And the commander of -- command of the 65th Protection Regiment. And also, on the top right corner, I see the initials or signature of Ziza, the communications officer from the Rogatica Brigade. Under the -- these initials are in Cyrillic under the number 1729.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we see that the same document was received by another unit, but I cannot recognise by which one. I cannot recognise the signature. But I am talking about document with ERN number 04258628. It was received by this unit on the 14th July 1995 at 2045.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, just to pick up on what you said a moment ago, sir, let's look at the upper left-hand corner of either of these documents, and we see the words "KOMANDA 1. PLP BR." What does that stand for? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, it's Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when we see this heading with the name of the brigade and then the strictly confidential number underneath and then the date underneath that, we see "dana" and then the date of 14 July 1995, when we see that heading, what does that tell us about what the source of this document is? What does that tell us about who is sending the document? And if that question didn't make any sense to you, sir, and I can understand if it didn't, I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you are referring to "dana." I don't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the document on the left, 65 ter 2025, with the ERN 04258576. How can you tell by looking at the top of this document who's sending the document and who's receiving the document? How can you tell that from looking at one of these VRS documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see on the left top corner this is the name of the unit which was from where the document was sent. And then we have listed the names of the units which should receive the particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And looking at this document, on the bottom of this document is handwriting here, "predato" [phoen], which means "sent," according to my knowledge of B/C/S, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So when we look at this document and we see at the top, and you've told us that "KOMANDA 1. PLP BR" means "command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade," otherwise known as the Rogatica Brigade, is that the sender or the recipient of the document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's the unit from which the document is being sent, and underneath it we have the names of the recipients; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just two more examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: 4069, please, and 4069B side by side. That will be 4069A and 4069B, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We've got two documents bearing strictly confidential number 18-250-1/1. And we can see a date of 28 July 1995. Again, this is the command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. What can you tell us about these two documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two documents coming from the same collection, from Drina Corps collection. The document on the right side of my screen with ERN number 04258567, it was -- it is document which was sent -- prepared by sender, in fact. It was sent to Main Staff, to IKM Drina Corps, and security organs of Drina Corps. And we see also on this document that this document was sent at 1530 hours, and we have initials of Ziza on the top right corner, under the number 1885. This is -- they are initials of or nickname of one of the communications officer from the Rogatica Brigade. And looking at the document with ERN number 04365051 we see, looking at the handwritings on the bottom of these documents, we see that these document was received on 28th July 1995, at 1715. And I cannot recognise the signature or initials of the man who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just focus for a minute on the document on the right ending with ERN 04258567, just to get us used to some of the B/C/S abbreviations that we're going to be seeing a lot of in the future. On the recipient lines on this document we see the letters "GSS VRS SEKTOR ZA OBP." What does that tell us about who that recipient is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Main Staff of Army of Republika Srpska, sector for security and intelligence, or intelligence of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when we have -- in that -- if I'm not mistaken, the "GSS" stands for "Glavni Stab"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This is B/C/S word or Serbian word of Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So when we see two S's like that, next to each other, that's for the "sh" in Stab?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the next recipient is the "IKM DRINSKOS KORPUSA."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This "IKM," this is "forward command post," abbreviation of the "forward command post" but, of course, in Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at two more documents, 65 ter 179 and 4072B, as in Bravo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We have two documents bearing strictly confidential number 12/45-975, dated 29 of July, 1995. What can you tell us about who is sending this document, just based on the heading? And I don't want to ask you about the substance of the document, but where is this being sent from?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sender of this document is Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, Glavni Stab VRS, and sector for intelligence. And looking at the serial number, this is sector for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And we see -- on the first line of the recipient we see the abbreviations "IKM DK," again. What's that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's forward command post of the Drina Corps on the hands of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The -- we see the letters N/L. Do you know what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's for General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That's "na licnost"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Na licnost," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Is that also -- does that mean personally to be delivered, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. It means this way, personally to be delivered to General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what can you tell us about the source of these documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of these documents are coming from Drina Corps collection, and I see on the list of the recipients also the command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, called Rogatica Brigade, and I talking about document with ERN number 04258566 --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, can we just scroll up just a touch on that document so we can catch the very top of that document. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the top of the right corner of this document, I see that this document was received at 2.45, on the 30th of July, 1995, it's in B/C/S, in Cyrillic, and I also recognise the signature of communications officer from Rogatica Brigade, Danko Gojkovic. He testified in the previous trial and he's our witness. And he recognised his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And have you personally met Mr. Gojkovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met him, but I think it was 2006 when we interviewed him, and then when he came to testify to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And maybe one or two more occasions, but roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 185, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, on this document if we can -- well, what can you tell us about this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also document from Drina Corps collection. These documents, in fact, were sent from Rogatica Brigade, as far as I know. I know it from communication officer from the -- from Rogatica Brigade, from Danko Gojkovic, whose signature is seen here also at this document, at the bottom of this document on the left side, in the left corner. And is saying here that this document was sent at 1510 hours. I don't think entire handwriting's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And looking at the top of the document where it says: "IKM 65. ZMTP." "Borike," and we see the number "1400," what does that tell you based on your investigation and reading this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is abbreviation of forward command post of 65th Protection Regiment. It was located in Borike, the village about 14, 15 kilometres, about 20 kilometres from Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you said a moment ago that this was sent from the Rogatica Brigade, where do you mean from when you say "Rogatica Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean from communication room of Rogatica Brigade. But referring to the testimony and to the statement of Danko Gojkovic, he told us that he doesn't remember exactly how he received this document. It could be through the courier or through the telephone. It was typed later on and he just transferred this document to the listed recipients from this document. But he sent it from Rogatica Brigade itself, but document was created, according to the title, at the 65th Protection Regiment forward command post in Borike.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I said, Mr. Gojkovic has been listed as a proposed witness in this case, Witness number 134, and I think actually he's been recently proposed to change from a 92 bis witness to a 92 ter witness. So that pleasure is yet to come for the Chamber, just to give a little background to that. Can we see who the recipients are for this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are commander of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska, for his information; assistant commander for the morale, religious, and legal affairs for the Main Staff of Republika Srpska; and commander of the military police battalion of the 65th Motorised Brigade -- Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- can we just put some names to those three titles?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska is General Mladic; the assistant commander for the morale, religious, and legal affairs of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska is General Gvero; I'm not sure about the commander of the military police battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll be hearing about that person at some point anyway. It's okay. Now, this document that we're looking at right now, when was the first time you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document very clear. First time I saw this document in Zagreb, when I made the initial assessment of the collection which arrived to Zagreb from Banja Luka. This document was one of the documents from the small binder. We called it "Atlantida," the binder, because on the cover page of this binder it was the word of "Atlantida," and I remember this document from this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With Madam Usher's assistance, I just ask that this bundle of documents be handed to the witness, and I'll ask him a couple of final questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please. But could you indicate which kind of documents these are.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, would you kindly remove the first item and --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Madam Usher, we'll need your further assistance with the ELMO, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just remove that first item from the folder and, if you would, place it on the ELMO. Perfect. Okay. What is this?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cover page of the binder I referred just a few seconds before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "binder," what kind of thing are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about few documents clipped together, and this is the cover page of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- this set of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can see two holes in this document, so is it fair to say this was a two-hole-punch, bound binder of documents; is that what it was?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. Now this is different shape because I see that the binder was divided for each document has separate folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So what can you tell us -- well, you've already told us this is from the Drina Corps collection and it's got an ERN of 04258544, for the record. I'll just ask you to replace that cardboard cover back in the folder, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the whole page be displayed. I would like to know whether there is anything hidden in the top part of the cover page. Can we see the whole page, not just one part of it. The top part is missing from the display. Can you scroll the document down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would replace that, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just for the record, we just saw the word "telegram" on the top of that document. What does that mean based on your investigation? What is a telegram and what can that refer to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch is telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd ask you to go to the end of that group of folders, and I think there should be ERN ending in 8580 there. Is that correct? And if you would, put that on the ELMO, please. And what is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document we saw just a while before. This is a document sent by Danko Gojkovic, created at the IKM of 65th Protection Regiment in Borike, and sent from Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you first saw this document, in what condition was it or how was it -- how was it packaged or otherwise held together?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told, this document and other documents from this pile were clipped together, they created -- they were kind of the binder. And the first page we saw just two minutes ago, it was the first page, the cover page of this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say this was the last page of the binder?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, thank you for taking us through that exercise, and I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Tolimir, do you have cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have a few questions. If you will allow me, I will like to cross-examine this witness, yes. Thank you. I would like to greet everybody in the courtroom once again, and I would like to welcome the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blaszczyk, you stated that, as a member of the international police force, you were deployed in the former Krajina or the "so-called Krajina in Croatia," that's what you said. My question is this: Where were you engaged, in what sector? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of my deployment to Croatia at that time, I was located in Sector North, so-called Sector North. Exactly I was in Petrinja, in the village or town called Petrinja, and it was few months -- the first few months of 1992. And then, temporarily, I was deployed to Sarajevo airport for two, three weeks. It was August 1992. And when I returned from Sarajevo, I stayed in Sector North for the next month or two maybe. And then from Sector North, from Petrinja, I was deployed to Sector West. It is Daruvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you saying that you were in the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina all the time? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was deployed -- most of the time I was deployed of the territory of the former Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaszczyk, which unit did you belong to? Could you please briefly describe your tasks in the Republic of Serbian Krajina? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, we were members of international police. It was monitoring mission, mission of United Nations, so-called part of UNPROFOR mission. And our task was monitor situation on our sectors and monitor the activity of the local police, but in fact, our access to the local police was very limited. In fact, we acted rather like humanitarian aid for the population in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Blaszczyk, what kind of duty did you have there? Were you an observer or were you the supervisor of some observer units? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty was monitoring duty. I was a monitor. I wasn't supervisor. I wasn't the station commander of our police, international police; I was ordinary monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Tell me why you said in your statements that you performed several duties in what you call the so-called or former Republic of Serbian Krajina, or, for short, Krajina. So why do you say Krajina in Croatia rather than Serbian Krajina? You even say the so-called Krajina.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that because I was deployed at that time a tour for this period, I was deployed to Sector North and Sector West, and shortly in Sarajevo. It means that condition of -- in each sector was little bit different, and my duty -- our duty or our presence over there was a little bit different then, for example, in Sector North than in Sector North [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this because in the agreement about the engagement of UNPROFOR in Croatia, the term "the so-called Krajina in Croatia" can nowhere be found, nor is it called "Krajina in Croatia." It -- either its proper name is used or the name that the UNPROFOR called, namely, sector whatever -- whichever it was. So please refer to it by any of these names that were in use while you were performing your duty there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked Mr. Blaszczyk why he was using terms to call the Republic of Serbian Krajina which were not in official use while he was carrying out the duties of an UNPROFOR member in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used the common name, the former Serbian Krajina or so-called Krajina because it doesn't exist anymore. This is Croatia now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, on page 58 of your testimony, line 2 into 3, you say "... in Sector North than in Sector North." I think you mean something different, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. You are correct. No, I meant Sector North and Sector West.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, tell us whether you officially received instructions from the United Nations not to do anything that could be interpreted as a recognition of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and not to use the name of that republic in your utterances.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such -- I don't remember such instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, were you engaged on several occasions in Bosnia-Herzegovina; and if so, please describe the nature of your activity there.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in 1992, I was deployed for two or three weeks to Sarajevo airport, and at that time we -- we were engaged to monitor the movement of the flights which were coming to Sarajevo with humanitarian aid and also movement of the passengers. And in 1996, I was deployed again -- not again, but I was deployed to Bosnia-Herzegovina as the member of IPTF, International Police Task Force, created also by UN mission, but UN mission for Bosnia-Herzegovina. But it wasn't part of UNPROFOR at that time, it was after Dayton Agreement in February 1996. And as I said during my first day of my testimony, I've been deployed to Bosnia-Herzegovina three times: The first time in 1996, then 1998, and 2001. Each time I stayed at least one year in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In 1996, I was deployed to Sarajevo and Vogosca; and then shortly to Herzegovina, to Mostar and Trebinje, but very shortly; and then to Bihac area, it was 1996. 1998 and 2000/2001, entire time I spent at Sarajevo -- in Sarajevo, in our headquarters, headquarters of IPTF mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You have already answered my other questions. Do I remember well that you said you started working for the OTP in January 2003, and where did you work before that? Did you work on military documentation, that is, did you investigate into military documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before I joined OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I mean the period preceding January 2003. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before that period I never -- before January 2003 I never worked with military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Before January 2003, did you have anything to do with police documentation?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean international police documentation or the local police documentation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I mean, did you work on archiving, registering, or any other activity that had to do with archives and documents, be it with the police or the military? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never involved in such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, what does training and monitoring the local police mean? That's an activity that you performed in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Training, it means typical training for the police officers. You know, according to the western Europe standards, let's say. And monitoring, it means that monitoring their activities, reacting on their reaction, how they did react for certain situation, events. And looking at their activities, we -- yeah, the IPTF prepares kind of training programme for the local police officers, but in fact, I never was involved in the training programme for the local police officers. I was involved in the job with IPTF HQ in Sarajevo. Mostly I was dealing with new monitors, new IPTF monitors, who were coming to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Before you got a job with the OTP, while you were monitoring the police force in Bosnia, did you -- did you have contact with any of their documentation for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 1996, when I was deployed to Mostar region, to Trebinje and then to Bihac region. I was deployed to the police station, the IPTF police station in these regions. And at that time we have contact with documentation from the particular police station from these regions. For example, the RS log-book we checked every day or every few days -- every day, I don't remember right now, who had been arrested by the local police or for what reason, et cetera, for example. And we were checking also the log-books of duty officers at the police stations, at the local police stations, checking what is the entries of the log-books. The only -- this is my only involvement with documentation from the local police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Tell me, did you ever analyse military documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I joined the OTP and the ICTY here, we are in constant contact with military documents, and obvious that we are analysing these documents, also me, in some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that you make assessments and analyses after having read those documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have my own assessment and analysis of such documents, but also we are using the help of our professional analysts to getting more information about particular documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us and describe the position in the OTP team for Srebrenica which you currently occupy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the investigator for this team. I am investigator for OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Tell us, please, as an investigator of the ICTY, what exactly are your duties? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty is to take the active part in our investigation regarding this subject, and I am interviewing the witnesses, victims, suspects, I am doing the suspects interview, I am collecting the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Before I pass on to my following question, please tell me: Do you have any legal experience in your work or do you have any legal training? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I graduated the police academy and I spent many years at our police, and I had a contact with legal aspects of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us whether your supervisor at the OTP is Mr. Peter McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Peter McCloskey, he is a senior trial attorney for this particular case, and generally, he is responsible for this case in -- it means that somehow I am subordinated to him in relation to this case. But my direct supervisor is deputy chief of investigation right now. Previously it was chief of investigation. I think now his title is deputy chief of trial support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you mean the chief investigator of the ICTY, Mr. Serge Brammertz or the chief investigator in this case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Se rge Brammertz is Prosecution -- the main Prosecutor for ICTY, but I meant the person who performed the duty as -- as deputy -- I think his title right now is deputy chief of trial support. His name is Bob Reid. And my direct supervisor is team leader of Team B, as investigation section was sometime ago divided for teams, A, B, C, D. I was a member of Team B and the head -- the chief of this Team B was Peter Mitford-Burgess, is still.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Can you, as an investigator of the OTP, publish the results of your investigations without the agreement of your supervisors in the OTP? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not possible. I should get -- this is possible of course, but I should get the permission from my supervisors.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, are you duty-bound to safe-guard the results of your activity or your investigations as an official secret? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as every investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This being the case, please tell us, can you make public appearances without the written permission of someone in the OTP; and if not, who is the one you need to apply for permission to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the procedure. I never was interested to ask for such permission, but I believe this is management of the OTP, of entire Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell me, is it your duty, as a member of the investigation team of the OTP, to protect -- to protect the interests of the OTP and harmonise your public appearances with the official positions of the OTP? And when I say "official positions," I mean the positions that the Prosecution puts forward in this trial. Thank you. I have been informed that the last part of my question has not been interpreted, so let me explain. When I say "official positions," I mean that you defend the allegations made by the Prosecution in the indictment as put forward in the -- in this trial? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite -- I would say that all of us, investigators and lawyers, we are obligated to disclose entire 68 rule evidence. And our rule as investigators, and I believe lawyers as well, is just to find the truth, exactly to find the real facts, what happened in this period we are investigating. It doesn't matter whether it -- sometimes it follows the first idea or theory of the Prosecution, but the most important is for us to find the facts and the truth, what had happened. Our position as OTP or, I believe, lawyers in our team can be changed if we find evidence telling or just telling a little bit different -- telling a bit differently than, let's say, the first idea, the first theory, OTP theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Speaking about what you have just explained, tell me, are you duty-bound as an investigator of the OTP to look for alleviating evidence in this case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell me which criterion do you apply to establish whether the evidence is alleviating. I'm referring to Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at the evidence I received or I managed to get, whether this evidence showing us a mitigation facts or exculpatory facts for that use. And in such occasion, if I manage to locate such evidence, we discuss, rather, this evidence with our lawyers and the evidence were put for disclosure log for the accused, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. If that is so, please tell us, can you, without a special permission of the OTP, testify as a Defence witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in fact, but I believe it's possible also.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me then, do you work full time as an OTP investigator on the team for Srebrenica or do you do some other work as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that I work full time for Srebrenica investigation, not necessarily for this case but mostly -- yeah. I investigate -- I am investigating or I am involved in investigation regarding the fall of Srebrenica in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Do you now spend as many hours doing the job as it was when you started, or can you give us a rough figure how many hours per month do you perform this work?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that we are spending much more hours than before, when I joined the OTP. It's difficult to say. I would say that this is unlimited working hours, almost. Sometimes we are starting our job at -- usually we should -- we are obligated to start our job at the office at 9.00 and it's very often we are sitting at the office long hours, having a lot of things to do, and also I spent many hours on the missions in the Balkans or other region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think it's time for the second break, and you should think about the course of questions you are putting to the witness, if it's really helpful for your Defence and your case to know exactly the kind of work and the time this witness is spending with his work in the OTP. You should use the break, the time of the break, to think about that. We adjourn and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please continue with your cross-examination, but do -- sorry, there was a mistake with the microphone. Could you indicate if you will be able to finish during this session today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I'll be able to because it depends on the witness as well, and I have a lot of questions. And I intend to use all the time that was allotted to me. I asked the gentleman about the number of hours that he spends investigating, and nobody will allow me an investigator. I would like to recall the principle of equality of arms. I have no investigator and you know how many the OTP have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this is a different topic. Now we are in cross-examination. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, before we move on to the second set of questions, tell us whether the OTP ever searched for ABiH documents in relation to the investigation about Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that such search has been done definitely, and I believe we got some quite useful documents from this search for our investigation. But I don't remember when it was done and where exactly, from the top of my head, but definitely it has been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, is there a collection of documents of the ABiH for those units that had anything to do with Srebrenica on your investigation team?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, you mean collection of the documents in our investigation team? We don't have such collections. We are using the collections seized by OTP or received from other sources, and everybody has access to these collections. And there are also documents from BiH army and BiH authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell me whether those documents and materials are accessible to the Defence team if we should apply for them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe yes. I don't see any reason why not, unless they are restricted documents, but it should be done in legal way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. You stated that the documentation of the Drina Corps comprises about 35.000 pages. Did you establish that personally or was it done by your fellow team members?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there are total about 315.000 pages, and it is easy to establish looking at their ERN range of the pages stamped by our evidence unit. But it was visible since the first I see -- I saw this collection in Zagreb, that this is big amount of the documents. But checking the exact number, it's necessary to look at the ERN range of these documents, Drina Corps collection documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. I made a mistake and said 35.000. It should be 315.000. Did you personally take part in the analysis of that documentation, such as its registering, listing, and processing? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each investigator whichever is taking part analysing the documents, it doesn't matter it is Drina Corps collection or other collection, having these document or using these documents by us, we have to analyse such documents. But regarding these documents from Drina Corps collection, we have some kind of the spreadsheet. One of our analysts created a spreadsheet and she is analysing each document from this collection. It takes long time to analyse each document from this collection, taking into the account how many pages there are. But so far as I remember, in our spreadsheet we have about 20.000 documents selected and put in the spreadsheet, you know, just particularly selected from the Drina Corps collections. I'm not talking about the pages, I'm talking about documents, 20- or 22.000 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, while you were preparing for this testimony did you review a number of documents, as we have been informed by Mr. Nelson, and my question is: Who selected the documents that you reviewed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Answering to the first part of your question, yes, I reviewed the documents which had been shown in this courtroom. And second part of the question, who selected the documents? There was a lawyer who conducted examination, of course, and -- yes. But to be clear, I seen these documents much before, before my preparation even for the Popovic case. When I testified in the Popovic case I seen these documents, most of them at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell us, what was the criterion for the selection of the documents that you reviewed before giving evidence here, or could you perhaps say more precisely why these documents were selected from the overall collection of 315.000.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We try -- I believe we managed to prove that these documents are authenticated. This is the criterion how we selected these documents from this collection. And yes, in this way. And showing the Trial Chamber also the way how the documents were handed over to us, the chain of custody of these documents, and also showing a little bit how the documents were distributed between the Drina Corps units and other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell me, were there also documents in that collection that are not reliable?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I don't remember any such document, seeing such -- any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Please tell me, all the copies of dual documents that have been shown here, do they all fully match content-wise?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't understand your question. Could you rephrase it, please. What do you mean by "fully match content-wise"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You have been examined about the circumstances connected to dual documents. There were differences in terms of numbering, et cetera, but are there any differences between these dual documents when it comes to their contents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say from the top of my head, but if I would have such documents in front of me, I would analyse the contents of the documents, of course I will notice the differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. For example, the first such document was P2775 -- 4 and P1982. They were shown to you at the same time. Did you analyse their form as well as the content, i.e., did you find any differences in the content just as you did in their form?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I look at these documents, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the General please repeat the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P2174 and P1982. These are the numbers, if I remember correctly, if I made -- 04312743 is the ERN number of the original, and the copy, 0917878 [as interpreted]. Thank you. Could these two documents please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to assist, Mr. President, I think we just need the -- I think what the General is asking for is the B/C/S original side by side, like we did before, rather than having the translation of the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a document issued by the Drina Corps on the 17th of July, 1995, and the original is number 0091785 -- actually, the copy is that number. And the original is 0425798. I still am not sure about the number because the document was not shown on the screen in its entirety. Can we please be shown the contents of that document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we have some confusion now. I really don't know to which document you are referring. During examination-in-chief the Prosecution used other numbers, and therefore that was quite simple. I don't know how to manage this problem now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Nelson knows which two documents he showed in parallel on e-court. Maybe he can assist. I could not make a note of the second number because I couldn't see the complete number on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can clarify the record just a bit, Mr. President. There is a reference that the General gave to 0425798. I think that's what's throwing us off. I think we can just disregard that number. What we are looking at now, I believe is what the General wants to look at. And on the left, we have 65 ter 2174, which bears ERN 04312743; and on the right, we have 65 ter 1982, which bears the ERN 00917878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the last number is really an 8 and not a 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The last number of the first page of the document is an 8; and the second page, the last number is a 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are these the documents you were asking for?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will make sure that my Defence team shows the document because I have just provided them with my notes kept in my own handwriting while the witness was being examined on chief. I will proceed and I'll move on to another topic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, the Drina Corps collection, did it also contain documents which did not belong to the Drina Corps? Could you please tell us whether you observed any such documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember such documents, but -- and not only documents, but also the few artefacts which were part of the Drina Corps collection. But I think there were documents of the Muslim army forces seized in Srebrenica after the Srebrenica was fallen or liberated by VRS. I remember these documents from this collection and also these few artefacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can you please now answer the following question: How come that the Drina Corps collection contained just one document of another unit and you still call the collection the Drina Corps collection? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are referring to these Muslim documents, I believe the documents was seized after the Srebrenica fallen, when Srebrenica was captured by the Serb army. If we are -- you are referring to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not referring to that, I'm referring to the original documents which originated from the Main Staff or from another unit; in other words, they were the ones considered incoming documents, not outgoing documents.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I understood your question clearly, but to my knowledge and my experience, I believe that it's possible that few Main Staff documents could be located in this collection because the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska were sending these documents to Drina Corps collection. And then from Drina Corps collection -- sorry, to Drina Corps command. And of course, from Drina Corps command, the documents were sent to subordinated unit of Drina Corps. And this is possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is possible for incoming documents, but how about outgoing documents sent from the main corps, the sabotage unit, and other such units which were not part of the Drina Corps? And I'm talking about a number of single documents from such units. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would prefer to see these documents which -- I would like to see what I am referring to, but I think -- yes. If it -- if this is possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I know what General Tolimir has in mind, but there's a -- the question refers to the main corps and the sabotage unit, and if we can just identify what we're talking about because I'm -- there's -- as far as I know, there's no such thing as the main corps. So if we could just have some specificity, I think that will help the record and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, could you deal with it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Mr. President. 04258580 is the ERN number of the document that was previously shown in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, your microphone is still switched on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If the General would like that to be shown, it is 65 ter 185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you now please switch off your microphone, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the -- we have now again the English translation. That was not what Mr. Tolimir had in mind. He would like, like in -- during examination-in-chief, to have the different type of the same document with different ERN numbers on the screen. Is that correct, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the left-hand side we can see the document that I asked for, and we don't see its copy, the one that Mr. Nelson showed. It is actually on the right-hand side. I'm going to use the left-hand side document, and you can avail yourself of the translation, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, to clarify, not Mr. Nelson is in the courtroom, but Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you now have a question for this witness, please ask him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, does this document originate from another unit? Is this the way units produce the documents, without any heading, without any military post? This looks like something that an elementary school student has written. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding this document, these documents was originated from IKM, the forward command post of 65th Protection Regiment in IKM in Borike, at 1400 hours. And indeed, this is not usual format of dispatches, but during the interview, communication officer from Rogatica Brigade, Danko Gojkovic, whose signature we have on the bottom of this document, confirm that he received this document. He doesn't remember whether this document was typed -- was dictated to him on the phone, as far as I remember, or sent by courier, could be from Borike IKM. Yes. But he -- for sure he recognised his signature and handwritings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Was the signatory of this document a Prosecution witness? Did you speak to him? Did he tell you anything about this document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to this witness. I interviewed this witness and also this witness testified in the previous trial, but I think he doesn't remember the contents of that document but he recognised his handwriting and signature here. And he is sure that this document had been sent by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This document does not bear a signature, and it is also not a handwritten document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct. It has no signature and this is not handwritten document, but not possible -- when we interview Mr. Danko Gojkovic, the communication officer from Rogatica Brigade, it is not possible that he could be sent any kind of private correspondence or whatever, you know, through the official communication channels. It should be given order to him to send this particular document. As I said, he doesn't remember exactly, but this document could be received by him for sending through telephone line or through the courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that you're talking about Gojkovic, but what did the author of this document say? In the Popovic case, there was a witness who claimed that he was the author of this document, so what did he have to say?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember from the top of my head, but you are referring, I guess, to Colonel Milomir Savcic, who testified in the previous trial. It's correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I did not want to mention his name. It's not up to me to mention the names of the Prosecution witnesses. You spoke to him, or rather, to all the Prosecution witnesses, and you're the ones who should tell us what they told you during the proofing sessions before the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- in fact, I don't remember whether I took the part in the proofing session of this particular witness, but I would prefer to see on an information report or proofing notes on this proofing session, if I can to refer to something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just so everybody knows, General Savcic is listed as a proposed witness for the Prosecution, he's witness number 128. So like Mr. Gojkovic, the communications officer we're talking about, we expect that testimony to be before the Trial Chamber from the horse's mouth, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think this is very helpful for your examination, to take that into account. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. And thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would now like to ask, Mr. Blaszczyk, is it logical that a telegram was sent to the following addresses: To the commander of the Main Staff; CC, the assistant commander of the Main Staff for morale and religious affairs; to the commander of the military police battalion, order. And then at the end of the document, an opinion and position is sought from a completely different person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is logical. This is logical that this dispatch was sent to the information for the commander of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska and to the assistant commander for the morale, religious, and legal affairs, Army of Republika Srpska, and order to the commander of military police battalion on the 65th Protection Regiment. Colonel Savcic, at that time, he was the commander of entire 65th Protection Regiment. It's obvious that the commander of the battalion of each regiment was subordinated to him, and as far as we know - also from the testimony of Colonel Savcic - the person who Colonel Savcic is referring to in his -- this document, I mean General Tolimir, was together with him at Borike at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Could you please read paragraph 4. He doesn't mention General Tolimir here, that's number one; and number two, why did he send this document to General Gvero in light of the fact that, in the chain of command, General Gvero was not his superior? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, would you like me to read it loudly, the fourth paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Tolimir asked you why you mentioned the name of General Tolimir in respect to paragraph 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see that there is referring -- Colonel Savcic is referring to the assistant commander for security and intelligence affairs of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, but this position was held at that time by General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I said that he didn't mention me under 4. How come that Savcic did not send this to his superior, but rather, sent it to General Gvero, who was not in a command position in that chain of command? He was not a commander of any unit in that chain of command. How do you account for that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From many documents we see that General Gvero was involved in the events following the fall of Srebrenica, and we see that he was in the chain of the command of the Srebrenica operation. And why he's referring exactly why he considered him as one of the recipients of these documents -- of these documents, I think you, General, and Trial Chamber will have opportunity to ask Colonel Milomir Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Did you see another document from the protection regiment addressed to General Gvero or to somebody else? Have you seen any other such documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember from the top of my head just -- but possible that I saw that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that some lawyers saw the Drina Corps collection. Did they also see this document and did they use it to defend their clients in other cases?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Before testifying in the Krstic case or in the case of any other generals, did you single out this and any such documents following the instructions of your team leaders?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't testify for the Krstic case. I testified in Popovic case only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this document used in the Popovic case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this document was used in Popovic case -- at least when Colonel Milomir Savcic testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was it used by the Prosecution or was it used by any of the Defence teams? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Prosecution for sure, but I believe it could be used also by Defence team. But we should go back to the transcript from Popovic trial to see who referred to these documents, but definitely was used by Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. We will look at that and we will deal with that when Savcic comes. Is it logical that only one document sent from the protection regiment should appear in the collection of what you call the Drina Corps collection? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told already, this is not complete collection of Drina Corps, and this is not collection of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. We know and everybody knows that 65th Protection Regiment, this is unit of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. And this is reason why we don't have more or at least I don't remember whether we have much -- many more documents from this unit. It could be still somewhere in the archive of the Main Staff. Unfortunately, we didn't manage to find the entire archive for the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you something else. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this. Is it logical that in the archives that you found in Gornji Milanovac you should find only one document originating from the regiment -- protection regiment which is very suitable for the Srebrenica trials, and I repeat, only one and not any others? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely this document was seized together with Drina Corps collection, and this is document, in fact, sent by the unit of the Drina Corps, by Rogatica communication officer. This is not surprise for me that the communication officer or -- or Rogatica Brigade had these documents of 65th Protection Regiment. We should remember that 65th Protection Regiment was operating at that time in Borike. This is area of responsibility of Rogatica Brigade and entire Drina Corps. And in fact, I should look at log of our Drina Corps documents to see whether we have more 65th Protection documents -- I mean, issued by the 65th Protection Regiment or not, but I don't remember now from the top of my head. But I remember very well this document because it was very significant document for me when I saw it first time in Zagreb in December 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we are running out of time. We are at the end of today's sitting. Mr. Tolimir, is it possible for you to indicate - I will not put any pressure on you - but to indicate how much additional time you would need for finishing your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most probably a minimum of two hours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And as the Prosecution had the opportunity to examine this witness for three hours, that was three times of the indicated one hour, it is the right, of course, of the accused to examine this witness. We are now in the position that we can't continue this week, we can't continue your examination next week because there's another witness scheduled which is -- was travelling, I think, from a far, distant, location. So that we shall find out the proper situation for you to come back to the hearing to continue the cross-examination. Thank you for your attendance here. We will just remind you that you should not contact either parties during -- about this -- the content of this case, but as you are a member of the OTP, you may, of course, contact your colleagues. We have one problem with the documents we have seen on the screen. You didn't tender them when they were on the screen, and although the Chamber -- you know the position of the Chamber, would appreciate that they were tendered when they were put to witnesses. Therefore, in this case I would prefer that you send a memo with the exact numbers, and then the Registry will give them exhibit numbers so that we have it as soon as possible on the record. In that way, we could really avoid some confusion which occurred now during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Mr. President. We have already distributed the list of documents to tender, so I think everybody has that and we'll deal with that when we meet again for the final tendering process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In this case, just very clear, if we would have the document, the Prosecution number, the exhibit number already on the record, it would be easier during cross-examination to use these documents. Please bear in mind that procedure in future cases. We have to adjourn now. We will resume next week, Monday, and then three Judges will be present again. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
